idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After checkout-api v2.3.1 went out, the service started failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are running v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying, and check why the unhealthy RC was promoted from staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the next steps. The first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident was opened and on-call was paged once.

The test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging, so it looks like a failing build got promoted to production anyway. Someone should find the root cause before v2.3.1 is deployed again.

- **Rollback:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the next steps. The first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that nothing had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident was opened and on-call was paged once.
